protected_content.objective: Repair the false rejection introduced by budget release without losing its accuracy and false-acceptance gains, then validate on genuinely fresh circuits.
completion_requirements: Repair the consumed 125-LUT circuit falsely rejected at cap128; do not use candidate IDs, labels or per-case lookup in inference.
Preserve budget-release MAE/MAPE and false-acceptance gains on retained development panels, including prior named subgroup repairs. Compare with both signed incumbent and budget-release candidate.
Freeze policy, cohort, finite candidate selection and acceptance gates before new labels; freeze selected weights and all test predictions before fresh synthesis labels.

On complete fresh circuits, require better MAE and MAPE than signed incumbent, no loss of budget-release accuracy gains, and no additional false acceptances or false rejections separately at caps32/64/128 against the appropriate frozen comparators. Report per-cap denominators and changed decisions.
Independently audit evidence, cached inference, source hashes, chronology and native measurements. Retain failures, negative results and all frozen previous artifacts.
Publish reproducible scripts, focused tests, exact results and research figures on latest; promote only if all predeclared requirements pass.
protected_content.interpretation: A failed experiment is progress but does not complete this goal. Fresh cohort results do not establish universal hardware safety or CPU performance.
